title.vi: Phiêu lưu tại quầy check-in sân bay

context_description.setting: International airport check-in counter at departure terminal
context_description.scenario: A traveler arrives at the airport check-in counter to get their boarding pass for an international flight. The check-in agent helps with luggage, seat selection, and provides important flight information.
objectives: Practice travel vocabulary (boarding pass, luggage, gate, departure)
Use polite request forms (Could I..., Would you mind...)
Practice present simple for schedules
Learn airport-specific phrases

role_persona.name: Sarah
role_persona.speaking_style: Clear and polite, uses professional airport terminology, speaks at a moderate pace for non-native speakers
role_persona.background: Sarah has worked at the international airport for 5 years and loves helping travelers from around the world.

vocabulary_list.definition: A paper or digital ticket that lets you enter the plane.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: I need to show my boarding pass to the agent.

common_error.wrong: I have a boarding passes for two people.
common_error.right: I have two boarding passes for two people.
common_error.why: Use a number before plural nouns, not 'a'.

vocabulary_list.definition: The process of registering at the airport before your flight.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: What time does check-in close for international flights?

vocabulary_list.definition: Bags or suitcases you carry when you travel.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: How many pieces of luggage can I check?

common_error.wrong: I have two luggages in my room.
common_error.right: I have two pieces of luggage in my room.
common_error.why: 'Luggage' is uncountable; use 'pieces of luggage' for numbers.

vocabulary_list.definition: The gate where you board your plane before leaving.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: What is the departure gate for flight BA 205?

common_error.wrong: Where is the departure's gate?
common_error.right: Where is the departure gate?
common_error.why: Use 'departure gate' as a compound noun without a possessive.

vocabulary_list.definition: A seat next to the airplane window.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: I would like a window seat, please.

common_error.wrong: I want to sit in the window's seat, please.
common_error.right: I want a window seat, please.
common_error.why: Use 'window seat' as a compound noun, not possessive.

vocabulary_list.definition: A seat next to the aisles in the airplane.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Could I have an aisle seat near the front?

common_error.wrong: I would like a aisle seat, please.
common_error.right: I would like an aisle seat, please.
common_error.why: Use 'an' before a vowel sound, not 'a'.

vocabulary_list.definition: An official document that proves your identity for travel.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Please show me your passport and boarding pass.

common_error.wrong: I lost my passport's yesterday.
common_error.right: I lost my passport yesterday.
common_error.why: Use 'my passport,' not 'my passport's' (no possessive 's').

vocabulary_list.definition: A journey by plane from one place to another.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: What time does my flight depart?

common_error.wrong: I want to go the flight to London.
common_error.right: I want to take the flight to London.
common_error.why: Use 'take a flight,' not 'go the flight'.

grammar_points.explanation: We use the Present Simple to talk about fixed timetables, such as flight departure and arrival times.
grammar_points.usage_in_story: The agent and learner use it to discuss when the flight leaves and when check-in closes.
examples: The flight departs at 10:30 AM.
Check-in closes two hours before departure.
The next flight to London leaves at 2:00 PM.

grammar_points.explanation: We use 'Could you...' and 'Would you...' to make polite requests instead of direct commands.
grammar_points.usage_in_story: The learner asks the agent for a seat change, help with luggage, or a printed boarding pass politely.
examples: Could you print my boarding pass, please?
Would you help me with my checked luggage, please?
Could I change to a different row, please?

conversation_flow.opening_prompt: Good morning! Welcome to Global Airways. How may I help you today?
key_milestones: Greet and ask for booking reference/passport
Provide boarding pass and gate information
closing_scenarios: Have a pleasant flight! Your gate is B12.
You're all set! Don't forget to be at the gate 30 minutes before departure.
Safe travels! If you have any questions, our staff at the gate can help.

suggested_prompts: I'd like to check in for my flight to Paris.
Could you help me with one piece of luggage?
Would it be possible to change my seat to row 15?

title.vi: Phỏng vấn xin việc thành công

context_description.setting: Modern office meeting room for a job interview
context_description.scenario: A candidate is being interviewed for a marketing position at a tech company. The HR manager asks about experience, skills, and motivation while the candidate demonstrates their qualifications.
objectives: Practice past tenses for describing work experience
Use present perfect for achievements
Learn job interview vocabulary
Practice formal business English

role_persona.name: Michael Chen
role_persona.speaking_style: Clear business English, asks follow-up questions, gives candidate time to think
role_persona.background: Michael has 10 years of experience in HR and enjoys finding talented people who fit the company culture.

vocabulary_list.definition: A document listing your work experience, education, and skills for a job.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: I updated my resume last week to include my project management experience.

common_error.wrong: I made a resume for apply for this position.
common_error.right: I made a resume to apply for this position.
common_error.why: Use to + base verb for purpose; for + gerund.

vocabulary_list.definition: The skills, education, and experience a job requires from a candidate.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Do you meet all the qualifications listed in the job description?

common_error.wrong: I have qualification for this position.
common_error.right: I have qualifications for this position.
common_error.why: Qualifications is usually plural when listing required skills and experience.

vocabulary_list.definition: A person who works well and cooperates with others in a group.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: I believe I am a good team player because I always support my colleagues.

common_error.wrong: I am a team player who work well with my colleagues.
common_error.right: I am a team player who works well with my colleagues.
common_error.why: Use third-person singular verb after who referring to a singular noun.

vocabulary_list.definition: The final date or time by which something must be completed.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: In my last project, I always met the deadline without any problems.

common_error.wrong: I was late to the deadline last month.
common_error.right: I missed the deadline last month.
common_error.why: You meet or miss a deadline; you are not late to it.

vocabulary_list.definition: The amount of money a candidate hopes to earn in a job.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Before we discuss salary expectations, could you tell me about your current role?

vocabulary_list.definition: A personal quality or skill that you are not very good at.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: When I was asked about my weakness, I said I sometimes take on too much work.

common_error.wrong: I have a weakness about public speaking.
common_error.right: I have a weakness in public speaking.
common_error.why: Use in after weakness to show the area, not about.

grammar_points.explanation: The Present Perfect connects past achievements to the present, showing they still matter now.
grammar_points.usage_in_story: The candidate uses it to highlight accomplishments that are directly relevant to the TechVision Inc. position.
examples: I have managed three major projects successfully in my last role.
She has increased team productivity by twenty percent over two years.
I have completed all the required certifications for this position.

grammar_points.explanation: The Past Simple describes completed actions at a specific, finished time in the past.
grammar_points.usage_in_story: The candidate uses it to narrate particular events and stories from previous jobs during the interview.
examples: I led a team of five people during the 2023 product launch.
Last year, I resolved a major client complaint within two hours.
I graduated from the University of Technology in 2019.

grammar_points.explanation: The second conditional (if + past simple, would + base verb) describes unreal or unlikely present situations.
grammar_points.usage_in_story: The candidate uses it to imagine how they would handle new challenges if they joined TechVision Inc.
examples: If I were given more responsibility, I would take it on confidently.
If the project deadline moved up, I would reorganize my schedule immediately.
If I joined TechVision, I would focus on improving our client communication.

conversation_flow.opening_prompt: Hello! Thank you for coming in today. I'm Michael Chen, the HR Manager. Please, have a seat. How are you doing today?
closing_scenarios: Thank you for your time. We'll be in touch within a week.
I'm impressed with your qualifications. HR will contact you soon.
Do you have any questions for me before we wrap up?

suggested_prompts: Could you tell me more about the team I would join?
I am excited about this opportunity and ready to start soon.
What does a typical day look like in this role?

context_description.setting: A cozy Italian restaurant in the city center
context_description.scenario: A customer visits a restaurant for dinner. The waiter takes their order, recommends dishes, and ensures they have a pleasant dining experience.
objectives: Practice ordering food and drinks
Learn food and restaurant vocabulary
Use 'would like' for polite requests
Practice countable and uncountable nouns

role_persona.name: Marco
role_persona.personality: Warm, attentive, passionate about food, enthusiastic
role_persona.speaking_style: Friendly and welcoming, makes food recommendations, speaks clearly and not too fast
role_persona.background: Marco has worked at his family's restaurant for 8 years and loves sharing authentic Italian cuisine with guests.

vocabulary_list.definition: A list of all food and drinks available at a restaurant
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Can I see the menu, please?

common_error.wrong: Can I see menu?
common_error.right: Can I see the menu?
common_error.why: You need 'the' before 'menu' because it is a specific thing.

vocabulary_list.definition: A small dish you eat before the main meal
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: I would like the tomato soup as an appetizer.

common_error.wrong: I want appetizer.
common_error.right: I would like an appetizer, please.
common_error.why: You need an article before a singular countable noun.

vocabulary_list.definition: The biggest dish of the meal, usually meat or fish
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: For my main course, I would like the pasta carbonara.

common_error.wrong: I want main course.
common_error.right: I would like a main course.
common_error.why: You need 'a' before a singular countable noun phrase.

vocabulary_list.definition: Sweet food you eat at the end of a meal
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: For dessert, I would like the tiramisu, please.

vocabulary_list.definition: The paper that shows how much you need to pay
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Could I have the bill, please?

common_error.wrong: Can I have bill?
common_error.right: Can I have the bill, please?
common_error.why: You need 'the' because there is only one bill.

vocabulary_list.definition: Extra money you give the waiter for good service
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Is the tip included in the price?

common_error.wrong: I give you tip.
common_error.right: I will leave a tip.
common_error.why: You need the article 'a' before 'tip'.

grammar_points.explanation: Would like is a polite alternative to 'want' used to make requests in formal or semi-formal situations.
grammar_points.usage_in_story: The learner uses 'would like' to order food and ask for the bill politely to Marco.
examples: I would like the pasta carbonara, please.
Would you like some wine to start?
I would like the bill, please.

grammar_points.explanation: Use 'some' in positive sentences and 'any' in questions and negative sentences with countable and uncountable nouns.
grammar_points.usage_in_story: The learner asks if there is any bread and requests some water during the meal.
examples: Could I have some water, please?
Is there any bread with the appetizer?
I don't have any allergies to the main course.

conversation_flow.opening_prompt: Buonasera! Good evening and welcome to Trattoria Marco! My name is Marco, and I'll be your waiter tonight. Here's your menu. Can I start you off with something to drink?
key_milestones: Take main course orders with recommendations
closing_scenarios: I hope you enjoyed your meal! Grazie and please come again!
Here's your bill. It was a pleasure serving you tonight!
Thank you for dining with us! Have a wonderful evening!

suggested_prompts: I would like to start with the bruschetta, please.
I am not sure what to order. Can you help?
I would like to pay now, please.

context_description.setting: A modern clothing store in a shopping mall
context_description.scenario: A customer is looking for clothes for a special occasion. The sales assistant helps them find the right size, style, and tries to understand their preferences.
objectives: Practice shopping vocabulary (size, color, style)
Use comparative and superlative adjectives
Learn how to ask for help and express preferences
Practice trying on clothes phrases

role_persona.name: Emma
role_persona.personality: Stylish, helpful, enthusiastic about fashion, patient
role_persona.speaking_style: Friendly and encouraging, gives honest fashion advice, uses size and color vocabulary naturally
role_persona.background: Emma studied fashion design and loves helping customers find outfits that make them feel confident.

vocabulary_list.definition: A small room where you put on clothes to check how they look.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Could you tell me where the fitting room is, please?

vocabulary_list.definition: The measurement that tells how big or small a piece of clothing is.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: What size do you wear, medium or large?

common_error.wrong: I wear a size of M.
common_error.right: I wear size M.
common_error.why: Do not use 'of' between 'size' and the letter or number.

vocabulary_list.definition: A reduction in the normal price of an item.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Is there a discount on these summer dresses?

common_error.wrong: I want a discount 20 percent on this jacket.
common_error.right: I want a 20 percent discount on this jacket.
common_error.why: The percentage goes before the noun, not after it without 'of'.

vocabulary_list.definition: To put on a piece of clothing to see if it looks good.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Can I try on this blue shirt, please?

common_error.wrong: Can I try on it?
common_error.right: Can I try it on?
common_error.why: Pronouns go between the verb and the particle in phrasal verbs.

vocabulary_list.definition: To be the right size and shape for your body.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Does this dress fit me well?

common_error.wrong: This shirt is fit for me.
common_error.right: This shirt fits me.
common_error.why: 'Fit' is a verb here, so use the -s form, not 'is + fit'.

vocabulary_list.definition: A paper that shows what you bought and how much you paid.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Could I have the receipt, please?

common_error.wrong: Can you give me receipt?
common_error.right: Can you give me a receipt?
common_error.why: Singular countable nouns need an article like 'a' or 'the'.

grammar_points.explanation: Comparatives compare two things (bigger, more expensive) and superlatives compare three or more (the biggest, the most expensive).
grammar_points.usage_in_story: The learner compares prices, sizes, or styles of different clothes while browsing the store.
examples: This dress is more expensive than that one.
Is this the cheapest jacket in the store?
This shirt fits better than the blue one.

grammar_points.explanation: Phrasal verbs combine a verb with a particle to create a new meaning related to shopping actions.
grammar_points.usage_in_story: The learner uses phrasal verbs like 'try on', 'pick up', and 'put back' while browsing the store.
examples: Can I try on this pair of jeans?
I'll pick up a T-shirt and then put it back.
Could you let me try on the red one?

conversation_flow.opening_prompt: Hi there! Welcome to StyleHub! I'm Emma. Are you looking for something special today, or just browsing?
key_milestones: Greet and ask what customer is looking for
Help find right size and style
Process purchase or help find alternatives
closing_scenarios: Great choice! You look amazing in that! Ready to check out?
Let me know if you need anything else. The fitting rooms are on your left.
Thank you for shopping with us! Enjoy your new outfit!

suggested_prompts: I'm looking for a summer dress in blue.
Do you have this in a smaller size?
How much is this jacket after the discount?

context_description.setting: A modern medical clinic with a friendly doctor
context_description.scenario: A patient visits the doctor with common symptoms. The doctor asks about symptoms, gives a diagnosis, and provides treatment advice.
objectives: Practice describing health symptoms
Learn medical vocabulary (symptoms, medicine, treatment)
Use present perfect continuous for duration
Practice giving health history

role_persona.name: Dr. Lisa Park
role_persona.speaking_style: Clear medical explanations simplified for patients, asks clarifying questions, provides reassurance
role_persona.background: Dr. Park has been a family doctor for 12 years and specializes in making patients feel comfortable and understood.

vocabulary_list.definition: A sign that something is wrong with your body.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: The main symptom I've noticed is a persistent headache on the right side.

common_error.wrong: I am symptom today.
common_error.right: I have a symptom today.
common_error.why: Symptom is a noun, not an adjective; use 'have' with it.

vocabulary_list.definition: A raised body temperature, usually above 38°C, caused by illness.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: I've had a fever of 39 degrees for two days now.

common_error.wrong: I have a fever of 39 degrees high.
common_error.right: I have a fever of 39 degrees.
common_error.why: Don't add 'high' after a specific temperature number.

vocabulary_list.definition: A written order from a doctor for specific medicine.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Could you write me a prescription for the antibiotics, please?

vocabulary_list.definition: A substance taken to treat or prevent illness.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: I take this medicine twice a day after meals.

vocabulary_list.definition: Pain or irritation in the throat, often from infection.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: My sore throat got worse after I swallowed hot soup yesterday.

common_error.wrong: I have sore throat since yesterday.
common_error.right: I have had a sore throat since yesterday.
common_error.why: Sore throat is countable and needs the article 'a'.

vocabulary_list.definition: A period of inactivity to allow the body to recover.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: The doctor told me I need at least two days of rest.

common_error.wrong: I need to do rest for a week.
common_error.right: I need to get a week of rest.
common_error.why: Use 'get rest' or 'take rest,' not 'do rest.'

vocabulary_list.definition: Having an immune reaction to a substance like pollen or food.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: I'm allergic to penicillin, so please avoid that antibiotic.

common_error.wrong: I am allergy to peanuts.
common_error.right: I am allergic to peanuts.
common_error.why: Allergy is a noun; allergic is the adjective form.

grammar_points.explanation: Use 'have/has been + verb-ing' to describe an action that started in the past and is still happening now.
grammar_points.usage_in_story: The patient describes how long their symptoms have lasted before seeing the doctor.
examples: I've been feeling tired for three days now.
She's been taking antibiotics since Monday.
I've been having trouble sleeping this week.

grammar_points.explanation: Use 'should + base verb' to give or ask for recommendations about health actions.
grammar_points.usage_in_story: The doctor advises the patient on treatment, and the patient asks what they should do next.
examples: You should drink plenty of water while you have a fever.
I should probably take the medicine before bed, right?
You shouldn't drive if you're feeling dizzy from this medicine.

grammar_points.grammar_structure: Present Simple for Habits and Routines
grammar_points.explanation: Use the base verb form to describe regular actions, routines, or general truths about health.
grammar_points.usage_in_story: The patient describes daily habits, and the doctor asks about lifestyle patterns to diagnose the issue.
examples: I usually take my vitamins in the morning.
She drinks about two litres of water every day.
Do you exercise regularly, or do you mostly sit at a desk?

conversation_flow.opening_prompt: Good morning! I'm Dr. Lisa Park. Please, have a seat. What brings you in to see me today?
key_milestones: Initial greeting and ask about symptoms
Ask follow-up questions about duration and severity
Ask about medical history and allergies
closing_scenarios: Take this medicine as directed. You should feel better in a few days.
Come back if your symptoms don't improve in a week.
Get plenty of rest and drink lots of fluids. Feel better soon!

suggested_prompts: I've been coughing every night for about a week now.
I should probably stop working out until this gets better.
I usually take ibuprofen for headaches, but it's not helping anymore.

title.en: Apartment Renting - Finding a New Home
title.vi: Thuê căn hộ - Tìm kiếm ngôi nhà mới

context_description.setting: Inside a rental agency or at a potential apartment viewing
context_description.scenario: A prospective tenant meets with a landlord or rental agent to discuss renting an apartment. They discuss terms like lease duration, security deposit, and utilities.
objectives: Practice housing and rental vocabulary (lease, deposit, utilities)
Ask about terms and conditions
Express requirements and preferences
Practice conditional sentences (If I move in early...)

role_persona.name: Mr. Harrison
role_persona.speaking_style: Clear and structured, uses real estate terminology, explains legal terms simply
role_persona.background: Mr. Harrison manages multiple residential properties in the city center.

vocabulary_list.definition: A written contract between a landlord and tenant that sets the rental terms.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Before you move in, I'll need you to sign the lease agreement.

vocabulary_list.definition: A sum of money paid upfront, returned at the end of the tenancy.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: The security deposit is two months' rent, and you'll get it back at the end.

common_error.wrong: How much is security deposit?
common_error.right: How much is the security deposit?
common_error.why: It refers to a specific deposit here, so it needs the.

vocabulary_list.definition: Ongoing costs like electricity, water, gas, and internet for the apartment.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Let me check whether the utilities are included in the monthly rent.

common_error.wrong: Are utility included in the rent?
common_error.right: Are utilities included in the rent?
common_error.why: Utilities is always plural in English for these services.

conversation_flow.opening_prompt: Hello! Are you here to view the studio apartment on the 3rd floor?
closing_scenarios: I'll think about it and get back to you.
Can I sign the lease today?

suggested_prompts: Could you tell me if the parking space is included?
I would like to schedule a viewing for next Tuesday.
Is the apartment available starting from the first of next month?

grammar_points.explanation: Could and would plus a base verb make requests more polite than can or will.
grammar_points.usage_in_story: The learner uses these to ask Mr. Harrison for information or to arrange viewings politely.
examples: Could you show me the kitchen and the bathroom?
Would you be available for a viewing on Saturday morning?
Could I see a copy of the lease agreement before I decide?

grammar_points.explanation: If plus present simple, will plus base verb describes a realistic future result of a condition.
grammar_points.usage_in_story: The learner uses this to ask what happens after signing or if certain conditions are met.
examples: If I sign the lease, when can I move in?
If the rent is too high, will you consider a lower amount?
If I pay the deposit today, will I get the keys this week?

title.vi: Phỏng vấn xin việc Kỹ sư Phần mềm

context_description.setting: A formal office setting or a video conference call
context_description.scenario: A senior developer is interviewing a candidate for a Software Engineer position. They discuss technical experience, architecture, and problem-solving.
objectives: Practice technical professional vocabulary (scalability, microservices, deployment)
Explain complex technical concepts clearly
Discuss past projects and challenges
Handle technical questions using the STAR method

role_persona.name: Alex
role_persona.speaking_style: Uses technical jargon correctly, asks challenging follow-up questions, focuses on architecture and logic
role_persona.background: Alex has been leading the platform engineering team for 8 years and has interviewed hundreds of candidates.

vocabulary_list.definition: The ability of a system to handle increased load without performance loss.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: One of my key responsibilities was ensuring the platform's scalability as user traffic doubled quarter over quarter.

common_error.wrong: We need to improve the scalabilitys of our platform.
common_error.right: We need to improve the scalability of our platform.
common_error.why: Scalability is uncountable; no plural -s is added.

vocabulary_list.definition: Accumulated shortcuts or suboptimal code that must be fixed to maintain system health.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: I led a sprint specifically to address the technical debt that had been accumulating in the payment module.

vocabulary_list.definition: Small, independent services that each handle one function within a larger application.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: After we decomposed the monolith into microservices, deployment times dropped from hours to minutes.

common_error.wrong: We built three microservice to handle the payment flow.
common_error.right: We built three microservices to handle the payment flow.
common_error.why: Microservices is plural; add -s after the number three.

conversation_flow.opening_prompt: Thanks for joining us today. To start, could you walk me through your most recent project and the technical challenges you faced?
closing_scenarios: We'll be in touch by next week.
Do you have any questions for me?

suggested_prompts: Could you walk me through your team's onboarding process?
I'd love to understand how you prioritize feature work versus refactoring.
What would my first month look like in your team?

grammar_points.explanation: Placing an adverb or negative phrase before the subject triggers subject-auxiliary inversion for emphasis.
grammar_points.usage_in_story: Used to highlight a standout achievement or an unusual professional experience during the interview.
examples: Not only did we reduce latency by forty percent, but we also cut infrastructure costs.
Rarely have I seen a team iterate so quickly on a complex distributed system.
Had the infrastructure been more resilient, the outage would have been far shorter.

grammar_points.explanation: A cleft sentence splits a clause into an It/What clause and a that/who clause to spotlight one element.
grammar_points.usage_in_story: Used to draw the interviewer's attention to a specific skill, project decision, or team contribution.
examples: What impressed me most about your stack was the emphasis on observability.
It was the migration to microservices that really tested my problem-solving skills.
What I'm most proud of is leading the team through that difficult release.

title.vi: Thời tiết và Kế hoạch trong ngày

context_description.setting: A casual morning conversation over breakfast
context_description.scenario: Discuss today's weather and make plans accordingly. This topic uses real-time weather data to provide an authentic experience.
objectives: Practice weather-related vocabulary
Learn to make suggestions based on conditions
Use future simple for plans
Master expressions like 'How about...?' or 'Why don't we...?'

role_persona.name: Alex
role_persona.speaking_style: Casual, friendly, uses common idioms about weather
role_persona.background: Alex always checks the weather before starting the day to decide whether to go hiking, surfing, or stay in a cafe.

vocabulary_list.definition: A prediction of the weather for the coming days.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: The forecast says it'll rain all afternoon.

common_error.wrong: The forecast is raining tomorrow.
common_error.right: The forecast says it will rain tomorrow.
common_error.why: Forecast is a noun; use says to report what it predicts.

vocabulary_list.definition: Having a lot of moisture in the air, making it feel sticky.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: It's so humid this morning, I'm already sweating.

common_error.wrong: The weather is very humidity today.
common_error.right: The weather is very humid today.
common_error.why: Humid is an adjective; humidity is a noun.

vocabulary_list.definition: Small, separate rainfalls that fall in different places, not everywhere.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: There are scattered showers in the afternoon, so bring a jacket.

common_error.wrong: There is scattered showers this afternoon.
common_error.right: There are scattered showers this afternoon.
common_error.why: Showers is plural, so use are not is.

conversation_flow.opening_prompt: Good morning! Have you seen the weather report for today yet? I was thinking of going out later.
closing_scenarios: Great, let's meet at 2 PM!
Maybe we should just stay home then.

suggested_prompts: I'm going to take the bus to work today.
Do you want to make pancakes for breakfast?
I need to call the plumber before noon.

grammar_points.grammar_structure: Going to + verb for future plans
grammar_points.explanation: Going to + base verb expresses a plan or intention you already decided to do.
grammar_points.usage_in_story: The learner uses it to tell Alex what they plan to do after breakfast or later in the day.
examples: I'm going to do the laundry this afternoon.
Are you going to work from home today?
I'm going to take an umbrella just in case.

grammar_points.explanation: The present continuous describes a planned, fixed arrangement with a specific time or person.
grammar_points.usage_in_story: The learner mentions a set appointment or scheduled activity for the day while chatting over breakfast.
examples: I'm meeting the landlord at ten.
I'm working from home this Friday.
Are you seeing anyone after lunch?

context_description.setting: Hotel reception desk in the evening
context_description.scenario: A learner practices a realistic hotel check-in conversation interaction. The conversation focuses on clear questions, practical vocabulary, and natural follow-up responses.
objectives: Use topic vocabulary for hotel check-in conversation
Practice asking for information and confirming details
Use polite requests with can and could accurately
Respond naturally to follow-up questions

role_persona.name: Maya
role_persona.speaking_style: Clear, natural, and level-appropriate with gentle corrections
role_persona.background: Maya has helped international visitors solve practical travel problems for years.

vocabulary_list.definition: A small key that opens your hotel room door.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Here is your room key, please keep it safe.

common_error.wrong: I lost room key yesterday.
common_error.right: I lost my room key yesterday.
common_error.why: Use 'my' or 'the' before 'room key' in this context.

vocabulary_list.definition: A code that identifies your booking at the hotel.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Could you tell me your reservation number, please?

vocabulary_list.definition: Arriving and getting your room before the normal time.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Is early check-in possible today, or do I need to wait?

vocabulary_list.definition: Leaving your hotel room after the usual checkout time.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Can I get a late checkout tomorrow, maybe until 2 p.m.?

common_error.wrong: I need a late check out.
common_error.right: I need a late checkout.
common_error.why: 'Checkout' is one word when used as a noun.

vocabulary_list.definition: A confirmed booking for a hotel room or service.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: I made a reservation last week under the name Tran.

common_error.wrong: I reservation a room last night.
common_error.right: I reserved a room last night.
common_error.why: 'Reservation' is a noun; use the verb 'reserve' here.

vocabulary_list.definition: The time you arrive at the hotel.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: What time is your arrival today?

common_error.wrong: My arrival is at 3 p.m. yesterday.
common_error.right: My arrival was at 3 p.m. yesterday.
common_error.why: Use past tense 'was' for a past time reference.

vocabulary_list.definition: The time you leave the hotel.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Your departure is scheduled for 11 a.m. tomorrow.

common_error.wrong: I will departure at 10 a.m.
common_error.right: I will depart at 10 a.m.
common_error.why: 'Departure' is a noun; use the verb 'depart' here.

vocabulary_list.definition: A written plan of your trip with dates and places.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Can I leave my itinerary with you for the next room?

common_error.wrong: I don't have no itinerary for this trip.
common_error.right: I don't have an itinerary for this trip.
common_error.why: Avoid double negatives; use 'an' before a vowel sound.

vocabulary_list.definition: A paper or digital proof for a flight, train, or event.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: I lost my flight ticket on the train this morning.

vocabulary_list.definition: A period when something is later than planned.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: There was a delay on the flight, so I arrived late.

common_error.wrong: The flight has a delay two hours.
common_error.right: The flight has a two-hour delay.
common_error.why: Use a hyphenated compound adjective before the noun.

grammar_points.grammar_structure: Polite requests with can and could
grammar_points.explanation: Use 'could' for more polite requests and 'can' for less formal ones in everyday conversation.
grammar_points.usage_in_story: The learner asks the receptionist for a late checkout, a room key, or confirmation of details.
examples: Could I have a late checkout until 2 p.m.?
Can you check if my room is ready?
Could you tell me the Wi-Fi password, please?

grammar_points.explanation: Use the past simple to talk about completed actions or events that happened at a specific time.
grammar_points.usage_in_story: The learner describes what happened before arriving, such as a flight delay or losing a ticket.
examples: My flight was delayed by two hours.
I lost my ticket on the train.
I made the reservation three days ago.

grammar_points.explanation: Use comparatives with 'than' to show that one thing has more or less of a quality than another.
grammar_points.usage_in_story: The learner compares the current room to a previous one or compares arrival and departure times.
examples: This room is bigger than the one I had last year.
Could I get an earlier check-in than 3 p.m.?
The departure time is later than I expected.

conversation_flow.opening_prompt: Hello! Welcome. How can I help you with your hotel check-in conversation today?
key_milestones: Clarify reservation number or early check-in
closing_scenarios: Thanks, that answers my question.
Great, I understand the next step now.
Could you send me the details in writing?

suggested_prompts: Could I please get a late checkout until three?
I'd like to confirm my reservation for Friday night.
My flight had a delay, so I'll arrive around midnight.

title.vi: Chu de: Asking for Directions Downtown

context_description.setting: Busy city street near a metro station
context_description.scenario: A learner practices a realistic asking for directions downtown interaction. The conversation focuses on clear questions, practical vocabulary, and natural follow-up responses.
objectives: Use topic vocabulary for asking for directions downtown
Practice asking for information and confirming details
Use present simple questions accurately
Respond naturally to follow-up questions

role_persona.name: Daniel
role_persona.speaking_style: Clear, natural, and level-appropriate with gentle corrections
role_persona.background: Daniel has helped international visitors solve practical travel problems for years.

vocabulary_list.definition: Go in the direction to your left side.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: You need to turn left at the big red building.

common_error.wrong: You must to turn left at the corner.
common_error.right: You must turn left at the corner.
common_error.why: After 'must', use the base verb without 'to'.

vocabulary_list.definition: A marked place on the road where people walk to cross the street.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Please wait here at the crosswalk for the green light.

vocabulary_list.definition: A place where you enter or exit the underground train system.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: The metro station is right next to this busy street.

common_error.wrong: I am going in the metro station to buy a ticket.
common_error.right: I am going to the metro station to buy a ticket.
common_error.why: Use 'to' for movement toward a destination, not 'in'.

vocabulary_list.definition: A famous building or place that is easy to see and remember.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: The tall clock tower is a good landmark to look for.

vocabulary_list.definition: A confirmed booking for a table, room, or seat.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Do you have a reservation at that restaurant near the station?

common_error.wrong: I have reservation for two people tonight.
common_error.right: I have a reservation for two people tonight.
common_error.why: Countable nouns need an article like 'a' or 'the'.

vocabulary_list.definition: The time or act of arriving at a place.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: My train arrival is at 3 p.m. at the main platform.

common_error.wrong: I am arrival at the station at 3 p.m.
common_error.right: My arrival at the station is at 3 p.m.
common_error.why: 'Arrival' is a noun; use 'arrive' or 'arriving' as a verb.

vocabulary_list.definition: The time or act of leaving a place.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: The departure board shows the next train leaves in ten minutes.

common_error.wrong: I departure from this city at 5 a.m. tomorrow.
common_error.right: I depart from this city at 5 a.m. tomorrow.
common_error.why: 'Departure' is a noun; use 'depart' as the verb.

vocabulary_list.definition: A written plan of your travel route and schedule.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Can I see your itinerary for the rest of the day?

common_error.wrong: I have itinerary for three days in this city.
common_error.right: I have an itinerary for three days in this city.
common_error.why: Countable nouns need an article; 'itinerary' starts with a vowel sound.

vocabulary_list.definition: A piece of paper or card that lets you travel or enter.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: You need a ticket to ride the metro from this station.

common_error.wrong: I will buy ticket at the machine over there.
common_error.right: I will buy a ticket at the machine over there.
common_error.why: Countable singular nouns need an article like 'a' or 'the'.

vocabulary_list.definition: A period when something is late or takes longer than planned.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: There is a delay on the metro, so the train is ten minutes late.

common_error.wrong: I am delay because the train is late.
common_error.right: I am delayed because the train is late.
common_error.why: Use the past participle 'delayed' as an adjective, not the noun.

grammar_points.explanation: Use 'do' or 'does' with the base verb to ask about routines, facts, or current states.
grammar_points.usage_in_story: The learner asks Daniel about the metro schedule and nearby locations using present simple questions.
examples: Does the metro run until midnight?
Do you know where the crosswalk is?
What time does the next train leave?

grammar_points.explanation: Use 'there is' with singular nouns and 'there are' with plural nouns to say something exists in a place.
grammar_points.usage_in_story: Daniel describes what the learner will see on the street to help them find their way.
examples: There is a big red building on your left.
There are two crosswalks near the metro station.
There is a landmark you can see from here.

grammar_points.explanation: Use the base form of the verb to give a direct instruction or command.
grammar_points.usage_in_story: Daniel gives the learner short walking directions to reach their destination downtown.
examples: Turn left at the crosswalk.
Wait here for the green light.
Go straight past the metro station.

conversation_flow.opening_prompt: Hello! Welcome. How can I help you with your asking for directions downtown today?
closing_scenarios: Thanks, that answers my question.
Great, I understand the next step now.
Could you send me the details in writing?

suggested_prompts: Excuse me, can you tell me how to get to the museum?
I'm looking for the metro station. Is it far from here?
Could you show me the way to the old clock tower?

title.vi: Chu de: Buying a Train Ticket

context_description.scenario: A learner practices a realistic buying a train ticket interaction. The conversation focuses on clear questions, practical vocabulary, and natural follow-up responses.
objectives: Use topic vocabulary for buying a train ticket
Practice asking for information and confirming details
Use polite requests with can and could accurately
Respond naturally to follow-up questions

role_persona.name: Priya
role_persona.speaking_style: Clear, natural, and level-appropriate with gentle corrections
role_persona.background: Priya has helped international visitors solve practical travel problems for years.

vocabulary_list.definition: The area where you wait for your train
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Which platform is my train on?

common_error.wrong: I am at the platform three.
common_error.right: I am at platform three.
common_error.why: No article before 'platform' plus a number.

vocabulary_list.definition: A ticket for a trip to a place and back
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: I would like a return ticket to Manchester, please.

vocabulary_list.definition: A ticket for one trip only, not back
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Is this a single ticket or a return ticket?

common_error.wrong: I need a single ticket to go London.
common_error.right: I need a single ticket to go to London.
common_error.why: You need 'to' after 'go' when stating a destination.

vocabulary_list.definition: The time when the train leaves the station
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: What is the departure time for the 5 o'clock train?

common_error.wrong: What is the depart time of the train?
common_error.right: What is the departure time of the train?
common_error.why: 'Depart' is a verb; you need the noun 'departure' here.

vocabulary_list.definition: A booked seat or place on a train
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Do I need a reservation for this train?

common_error.wrong: I make a reservation yesterday.
common_error.right: I made a reservation yesterday.
common_error.why: Past events need past simple, not present simple.

vocabulary_list.definition: The time or place where you get to your destination
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: What time is the arrival at Manchester station?

common_error.wrong: The train arrival at 5 pm.
common_error.right: The train arrival is at 5 pm.
common_error.why: 'Arrival' is a noun, so you need a verb like 'is'.

vocabulary_list.definition: The time or place where the train leaves
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: The departure is at 8:30 from platform four.

vocabulary_list.definition: A plan showing all your travel stops and times
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Can I see my itinerary before I pay?

common_error.wrong: I have a itinerary for my trip.
common_error.right: I have an itinerary for my trip.
common_error.why: Use 'an' before words starting with a vowel sound.

vocabulary_list.definition: A paper or card that lets you travel on a train
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Here is your ticket. Please keep it safe.

common_error.wrong: I buy two ticket for my family.
common_error.right: I buy two tickets for my family.
common_error.why: Use the plural form after numbers greater than one.

vocabulary_list.definition: When a train is late and leaves later than planned
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Is there a delay on the 9 o'clock train?

common_error.wrong: There is delay on the morning train.
common_error.right: There is a delay on the morning train.
common_error.why: 'Delay' is countable, so it needs an article.

grammar_points.grammar_structure: Polite requests with can and could
grammar_points.explanation: Could is more polite than can when asking someone to do something for you.
grammar_points.usage_in_story: The learner uses 'could' and 'can' to politely ask the ticket agent for tickets, information, or changes to a booking.
examples: Could I have a return ticket to London, please?
Can you tell me the departure time?
Could you check if I have a reservation?

grammar_points.explanation: Past simple describes actions that happened at a specific time in the past.
grammar_points.usage_in_story: The learner mentions a previous trip or a past booking to explain why they need help at the counter.
examples: I bought a ticket yesterday but I lost it.
The train arrived late last night.
I made a reservation two weeks ago.

grammar_points.explanation: Comparatives compare two things using -er or 'more' plus an adjective.
grammar_points.usage_in_story: The learner compares two trains or ticket options to decide which one to choose.
examples: Is the 9 o'clock train faster than the 10 o'clock one?
A return ticket is cheaper than two single tickets.
Is this platform closer to the exit?

conversation_flow.opening_prompt: Hello! Welcome. How can I help you with your buying a train ticket today?
key_milestones: Clarify return ticket or single ticket
closing_scenarios: Thanks, that answers my question.
Great, I understand the next step now.
Could you send me the details in writing?

suggested_prompts: Could I get a single ticket to Bristol, please?
I need to check my reservation for next Tuesday.
Can you tell me if there is any delay today?

context_description.scenario: A learner practices a realistic lost luggage claim interaction. The conversation focuses on clear questions, practical vocabulary, and natural follow-up responses.
objectives: Use topic vocabulary for lost luggage claim
Practice asking for information and confirming details
Use present perfect for experience accurately
Respond naturally to follow-up questions

role_persona.name: Omar
role_persona.speaking_style: Clear, natural, and level-appropriate with gentle corrections
role_persona.background: Omar has helped international visitors solve practical travel problems for years.

vocabulary_list.definition: The area where passengers collect their bags after landing.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: I've been waiting at the baggage claim for over an hour.

common_error.wrong: I go to baggage claim.
common_error.right: I go to the baggage claim.
common_error.why: Use the definite article before a specific place name.

vocabulary_list.definition: Written details about what your suitcase looks like.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Can you help me with the suitcase description on this form?

common_error.wrong: I need suitcase description.
common_error.right: I need a suitcase description.
common_error.why: Use an article before a singular countable noun.

vocabulary_list.definition: A document you fill in to report lost luggage.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: I'd like to fill in a claim form, please.

vocabulary_list.definition: A code that identifies your bag in the system.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: I have my tracking number here on my phone.

common_error.wrong: I lose my tracking number yesterday.
common_error.right: I lost my tracking number yesterday.
common_error.why: Use past simple for a finished action at a specific past time.

vocabulary_list.definition: A confirmed booking for a flight or hotel.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: I made a reservation under the name Tran.

common_error.wrong: I book a reservation for my flight.
common_error.right: I make a reservation for my flight.
common_error.why: We say 'make a reservation,' not 'book a reservation.'

vocabulary_list.definition: The time a flight reaches its destination.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: My arrival was supposed to be at 3 p.m.

common_error.wrong: I arrival at 10 o'clock.
common_error.right: I arrive at 10 o'clock.
common_error.why: Arrival is a noun; use the verb arrive instead.

vocabulary_list.definition: The time a flight leaves the airport.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: The departure time was changed to 6 a.m.

common_error.wrong: I departure from Hanoi at 8.
common_error.right: I depart from Hanoi at 8.
common_error.why: Departure is a noun; use the verb depart instead.

vocabulary_list.definition: A written plan showing your travel schedule and stops.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Can I show you my itinerary to confirm the flight?

common_error.wrong: I don't have no itinerary.
common_error.right: I don't have an itinerary.
common_error.why: Don't use two negatives in the same sentence in English.

vocabulary_list.definition: A document that proves you have paid for a journey.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: I still have my ticket in my handbag.

vocabulary_list.definition: When a flight is late and leaves later than planned.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Is there a delay on my flight?

common_error.wrong: My flight is delay.
common_error.right: My flight is delayed.
common_error.why: Use the past participle after 'is' to make passive voice.

grammar_points.explanation: We use present perfect to talk about past events that still have a connection to the present moment.
grammar_points.usage_in_story: The learner uses it to describe what they have or haven't done with their luggage up to now.
examples: I have already checked my bag at the counter.
I haven't seen my suitcase yet.
Have you ever lost a bag before?

grammar_points.explanation: We use first conditional to talk about real possible future situations and their likely results.
grammar_points.usage_in_story: The learner uses it to ask what will happen next or to set conditions for getting their bag back.
examples: If you find my bag, please call this number.
If my luggage doesn't arrive, I will need new clothes.
What will you do if the tracking number doesn't work?

grammar_points.explanation: We use modals like should, could, and ought to give or ask for advice about what to do.
grammar_points.usage_in_story: The agent gives suggestions about next steps, and the learner asks for recommendations.
examples: You should keep your receipt until the bag is found.
Could you tell me what I should do next?
I think you should file a claim form today.

conversation_flow.opening_prompt: Hello! Welcome. How can I help you with your lost luggage claim today?
key_milestones: Clarify suitcase description or claim form
closing_scenarios: Thanks, that answers my question.
Great, I understand the next step now.
Could you send me the details in writing?

suggested_prompts: I haven't seen my suitcase yet and I'm worried.
Could you help me report my lost bag, please?
I need to know when my luggage will arrive.

title.vi: Chu de: Customs and Immigration Questions

context_description.scenario: A learner practices a realistic customs and immigration questions interaction. The conversation focuses on clear questions, practical vocabulary, and natural follow-up responses.
objectives: Use topic vocabulary for customs and immigration questions
Practice asking for information and confirming details
Use present perfect for experience accurately
Respond naturally to follow-up questions

role_persona.name: Elena
role_persona.speaking_style: Clear, natural, and level-appropriate with gentle corrections
role_persona.background: Elena has helped international visitors solve practical travel problems for years.

vocabulary_list.definition: The reason you are coming to the country.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Please write your purpose of visit on the arrival card.

common_error.wrong: My purpose of visit are tourism.
common_error.right: My purpose of visit is tourism.
common_error.why: The subject is singular, so use 'is'.

vocabulary_list.definition: A form listing the goods you bring into a country.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Did you fill in the customs declaration on the plane?

common_error.wrong: I already filled the customs declaration yesterday on plane.
common_error.right: I already filled in the customs declaration on the plane.
common_error.why: Say 'fill in' a form, and use 'the' before 'plane'.

vocabulary_list.definition: An official permission to enter and stay in a country.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Your visa allows you to stay for thirty days.

common_error.wrong: I have visa for three months.
common_error.right: I have a visa for three months.
common_error.why: 'Visa' is countable, so it needs 'a'.

vocabulary_list.definition: How long you will remain in the country.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: What is the duration of stay on your application?

common_error.wrong: My duration of stay is during two weeks.
common_error.right: My duration of stay is two weeks.
common_error.why: Do not add 'during' before a length of time here.

vocabulary_list.definition: A booking that keeps a room or seat for you.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Can you show me your hotel reservation, please?

common_error.wrong: I booked a reservation in a hotel near to the beach.
common_error.right: I made a reservation at a hotel near the beach.
common_error.why: Say 'make a reservation at', and 'near' without 'to'.

vocabulary_list.definition: The act of reaching a place, such as a country.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Write today's date as your date of arrival.

common_error.wrong: After my arrival to Hanoi, I will call you.
common_error.right: After my arrival in Hanoi, I will call you.
common_error.why: Use 'arrival in' a city or country.

vocabulary_list.definition: The act of leaving a place to start a journey.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Your departure is scheduled for next Friday evening.

common_error.wrong: My departure flight leave at nine o'clock.
common_error.right: My departure flight leaves at nine o'clock.
common_error.why: With a singular subject, add -s to the verb.

vocabulary_list.definition: A plan of the places you will visit and when.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: My itinerary includes three days in Da Nang.

common_error.wrong: Can I see your itinerary? Yes, here are it.
common_error.right: Can I see your itinerary? Yes, here it is.
common_error.why: Say 'here it is' for one thing.

vocabulary_list.definition: A document that shows you paid for a journey.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Do you have a return ticket to your home country?

common_error.wrong: I have bought the ticket yesterday.
common_error.right: I bought the ticket yesterday.
common_error.why: Use the past simple with 'yesterday'.

vocabulary_list.definition: A period when something happens later than planned.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: There was a long delay because of the storm.

common_error.wrong: My flight was delay for two hours.
common_error.right: My flight was delayed for two hours.
common_error.why: Use the past participle 'delayed' after 'was'.

grammar_points.explanation: Use have or has plus a past participle to talk about life experiences without saying exactly when.
grammar_points.usage_in_story: The officer asks if you have visited the country before.
examples: Have you ever been to Vietnam before?
I have travelled to Thailand twice.

grammar_points.explanation: Use if plus the present simple, then will plus a base verb, for a likely future result.
grammar_points.usage_in_story: The officer explains what will happen if a rule is broken.
examples: If you stay longer than thirty days, you will need a new visa.
If your bag has food in it, we will check it.

grammar_points.explanation: Use should or ought to plus a base verb to give advice.
grammar_points.usage_in_story: The officer tells you what you should do next.
examples: You should keep your passport with you at all times.
You ought to declare the cash at the red counter.

conversation_flow.opening_prompt: Hello! Welcome. How can I help you with your customs and immigration questions today?
closing_scenarios: Thanks, that answers my question.
Great, I understand the next step now.
Could you send me the details in writing?

suggested_prompts: I'm here on holiday for two weeks.
Here is my passport and my return ticket.
Do I need to declare these gifts for my family?

Practice asking for information and confirming details

Respond naturally to follow-up questions

role_persona.name: Leo
role_persona.speaking_style: Clear, natural, and level-appropriate with gentle corrections
role_persona.background: Leo has helped international visitors solve practical travel problems for years.

vocabulary_list.definition: A tour where a person leads you and explains places.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: The guided tour starts at 10 o'clock in the morning.

common_error.wrong: I want to go a guided tour.
common_error.right: I want to go on a guided tour.
common_error.why: Go on is the correct preposition with tour.

vocabulary_list.definition: The place where the tour bus or guide meets you.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: The pickup point is right next to the main square.

vocabulary_list.definition: A tour you do on foot, visiting places step by step.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: I prefer a walking tour because I like to see everything.

vocabulary_list.definition: A ticket that lets you enter several museums for one price.

common_error.wrong: I want buy museum pass for today.
common_error.right: I want to buy a museum pass for today.
common_error.why: Use to before the verb and a before the noun.

vocabulary_list.definition: A booking you make in advance for a specific time.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: I made a reservation for the 2 p.m. tour yesterday.

vocabulary_list.definition: The time or act of arriving at a place.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: My arrival in the city was at 9 a.m.

common_error.wrong: What is your arrive time?
common_error.right: What is your arrival time?
common_error.why: Use the noun arrival before another noun.

vocabulary_list.definition: The time or act of leaving a place.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: The departure time is 4 p.m., so we need to leave now.

common_error.wrong: The departure is at the 4 o'clock.
common_error.right: The departure is at 4 o'clock.

vocabulary_list.definition: A list of all the places and times for your trip.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Can I see the itinerary for tomorrow's tour?

common_error.wrong: Can you show me your itinerant?
common_error.right: Can you show me your itinerary?

vocabulary_list.definition: A piece of paper or code that lets you enter an event.

common_error.wrong: How much is the tickets?
common_error.right: How much is the ticket?

vocabulary_list.definition: A period of time when something is later than planned.

common_error.wrong: There is a delayed because of rain.
common_error.right: There is a delay because of rain.

grammar_points.grammar_structure: Polite requests with can and could
grammar_points.explanation: Can and could are modal verbs used to ask for something politely, with could sounding slightly more formal.
grammar_points.usage_in_story: The learner uses these forms to ask Leo about tour times, availability, and details at the information center.
examples: Could you tell me what time the tour starts?
Can I see the map of the route?
Could you check if there are seats left?

grammar_points.explanation: The past simple describes completed actions in the past, formed with the base verb plus -ed or an irregular form.
grammar_points.usage_in_story: The learner mentions when they arrived or what they did before booking, and Leo confirms past reservations.
examples: I arrived at the center at 9 a.m.
She called me yesterday to confirm the booking.
I booked the tour two days ago.

grammar_points.explanation: Comparatives use -er or more to compare two things, showing one has more or less of a quality than the other.
grammar_points.usage_in_story: The learner compares tour options such as the walking tour versus the bus tour, or different departure times.
examples: The walking tour is cheaper than the bus tour.
Is the evening tour longer than the morning one?
This route is more interesting than the other one.

vocabulary_list.definition: An official card that allows you to drive a vehicle legally.

common_error.right: Do you have a driver's license?

vocabulary_list.definition: A choice of coverage plan for accidents or damage to the car.

vocabulary_list.definition: The rules about how and when you must refuel the rental car.

common_error.wrong: What is the fuel's policy for this car?
common_error.right: What is the fuel policy for this car?

vocabulary_list.definition: A check of the car's condition before you drive away.

common_error.wrong: I need to do a vehicle's inspection now.
common_error.right: I need to do a vehicle inspection now.

vocabulary_list.definition: A booking you made in advance to rent a specific car.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: I made a reservation online for a compact car this weekend.

vocabulary_list.definition: The time you are expected to pick up the rental car.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: What time is your scheduled arrival at the agency?

common_error.wrong: My arrive is at three p.m.
common_error.right: My arrival is at three p.m.
common_error.why: 'Arrive' is a verb; the noun form is 'arrival'.

vocabulary_list.definition: The time you are scheduled to return the rental car.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Your departure is set for six p.m. on Friday.

common_error.wrong: What is my depart time?
common_error.right: What is my departure time?

vocabulary_list.definition: A written plan listing your travel stops and dates.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Could you share your itinerary so I can suggest a suitable vehicle?

vocabulary_list.definition: A document proving your booking, often a confirmation email or code.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Please show me your booking ticket or confirmation number.

vocabulary_list.definition: A period of waiting because something is later than planned.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: I'm sorry for the delay; our system was down this morning.

common_error.wrong: There is a delay's of two hours.
common_error.right: There is a delay of two hours.
common_error.why: No possessive 's' is needed after 'a delay'.

grammar_points.explanation: The present perfect (have/has + past participle) describes life experiences up to now without specifying when they happened.
grammar_points.usage_in_story: The learner tells the agent whether they have rented a car before or have driven in unfamiliar areas, establishing their experience level.
examples: I have never rented a car in another country.
Have you ever handled a vehicle inspection before?
I have driven in heavy traffic many times.

grammar_points.explanation: The first conditional (if + present simple, will + base verb) talks about real, possible future situations and their results.
grammar_points.usage_in_story: The agent explains consequences of arriving late or choosing a different fuel policy, and the learner asks about possible outcomes.
examples: If you arrive after six p.m., we will charge an extra fee.
If I return the car early, will you reduce the price?
If the fuel is below half, you will pay a refueling charge.

grammar_points.explanation: Modals such as should, ought to, or had better are used to give recommendations or suggestions.
grammar_points.usage_in_story: The agent advises the learner on which insurance option to pick, what to check during the vehicle inspection, and how to handle a delay.
examples: You should choose the full-coverage insurance option for peace of mind.
You had better check the vehicle inspection form carefully.
You should download a map before your departure.

role_persona.speaking_style: Clear, natural, and level-appropriate with gentle corrections
role_persona.background: Grace keeps questions direct, calm, and focused on safety information.

vocabulary_list.definition: A passport you can no longer find because you misplaced or someone stole it.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: I need to report my lost passport to the local police station first.

common_error.wrong: I losted my passport this morning.
common_error.right: I lost my passport this morning.
common_error.why: Lost is irregular; the past form stays lost, not losted.

vocabulary_list.definition: A person you call when something serious happens and you need urgent help.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Could you please call my emergency contact in Vietnam to let them know I'm safe?

common_error.wrong: I need to emergency contact my family right now.
common_error.right: I need to call my emergency contact in my family right now.
common_error.why: Emergency contact is a noun, not a verb you can use directly.

vocabulary_list.definition: An official written document from police recording details of an incident.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: You'll need the police report to apply for a replacement passport at the embassy.

vocabulary_list.definition: A short-term official paper proving your identity until a new one is issued.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: The embassy can issue you a temporary document so you can fly home tomorrow.

common_error.wrong: I need to apply a temporary document from your office.
common_error.right: I need to apply for a temporary document from your office.
common_error.why: Apply needs for when you are requesting something from an authority.

vocabulary_list.definition: To give official information about an incident to an authority.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: You should report the theft to the local police as soon as possible.

common_error.wrong: I need to report about my stolen bag to the officer.
common_error.right: I need to report my stolen bag to the officer.
common_error.why: Report is transitive here; no preposition about is needed.

vocabulary_list.definition: The specific place or position where someone or something is.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Can you tell me the exact location where you last had your bag?

common_error.wrong: I don't know the location of where my passport was.
common_error.right: I don't know the location where my passport was.
common_error.why: Location already means place; of where is redundant.

vocabulary_list.definition: A detailed account of what a person or thing looks like.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: The police officer asked for a full description of the man who took your bag.

common_error.wrong: Can you give me a description about the thief?
common_error.right: Can you give me a description of the thief?
common_error.why: Use description of, not description about, for identifying details.

vocabulary_list.definition: Physical harm or damage to a person's body.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Is there any injury you sustained during the incident, or are you physically okay?

common_error.wrong: I have a injury on my arm from the fall.
common_error.right: I have an injury on my arm from the fall.
common_error.why: Injury starts with a vowel sound, so use an not a.

vocabulary_list.definition: Help or support given to someone in a difficult situation.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Our office provides free assistance to citizens who are in trouble abroad.

vocabulary_list.definition: A person who saw an event or incident happen firsthand.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Did you find any witness who saw the man take your bag?

common_error.wrong: There was a witness saw the accident happen.
common_error.right: There was a witness who saw the accident happen.
common_error.why: You need a relative pronoun who to connect the two clauses.

grammar_points.explanation: Used for hypothetical present or future situations, formed with if + past simple, would + base verb.
grammar_points.usage_in_story: The learner imagines consequences of not having a passport, and Grace explains what would happen under different conditions at the embassy.
examples: If I didn't have my passport, I wouldn't be able to board the flight home.
What would you do if you lost your documents in a foreign country?
If the embassy were closed, we would need to wait until Monday for assistance.

grammar_points.explanation: Used when focus is on the action or receiver, not the doer, formed with be + past participle.
grammar_points.usage_in_story: Grace explains procedures where the passport, document, or report is the focus rather than who performs the action.
examples: Your lost passport must be reported to the police within 24 hours.
A temporary document will be issued to you by the consular office.
The police report should be submitted before you apply for a replacement.

grammar_points.explanation: Clauses starting with a relative pronoun that add extra information about a previously mentioned noun.
grammar_points.usage_in_story: Used to describe the person who lost the passport, the place where it was lost, or the document that is needed.
examples: The person who lost their passport needs to come to the embassy in person.
This is the form that you need to fill out before we can help you.
The hotel where you stayed can confirm your location to the police.

key_milestones: Clarify emergency contact or police report
closing_scenarios: Thanks, that answers my question.
Great, I understand the next step now.
Could you send me the details in writing?

suggested_prompts: I lost my passport yesterday and I really need help.
Could you tell me what documents I should bring?
I'm scared I can't travel home without a passport.

role_persona.name: Ethan
role_persona.speaking_style: Clear, natural, and level-appropriate with gentle corrections
role_persona.background: Ethan leads professional conversations with clear expectations and supportive feedback.

vocabulary_list.definition: A problem that stops you from finishing your work.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: I have a blocker with the database access right now.

common_error.wrong: I have blocker with the login system.
common_error.right: I have a blocker with the login system.
common_error.why: Blocker is a countable noun, so it needs an article.

vocabulary_list.definition: A short report on how your work is going.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Let me give a quick progress update on the login feature.

common_error.wrong: I will give progress update this morning.
common_error.right: I will give a progress update this morning.
common_error.why: Progress update is a countable noun phrase, so it needs 'a'.

vocabulary_list.definition: The main aim your team wants to reach this sprint.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Are we still on track to meet the sprint goal by Friday?

vocabulary_list.definition: The thing you will do after your current work.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: My next task is to write the API documentation.

common_error.wrong: I will do a next task tomorrow.
common_error.right: I will do the next task tomorrow.
common_error.why: Next is superlative-like, so it takes 'the', not 'a'.

vocabulary_list.definition: The last date or time to finish something.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: The deadline for the design review is next Wednesday.

common_error.wrong: I will arrive the deadline on Friday.
common_error.right: I will meet the deadline on Friday.
common_error.why: Meet a deadline is the correct collocation, not 'arrive'.

vocabulary_list.definition: The most important thing to do first.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Fixing the bug is my top priority this week.

common_error.wrong: I am priority this task.
common_error.right: This task is my priority.
common_error.why: Priority is a noun, not a verb; use 'is' to describe it.

vocabulary_list.definition: Comments or opinions from others about your work.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Could you give me some feedback on the new layout?

common_error.wrong: I received two feedbacks from the client.
common_error.right: I received two pieces of feedback from the client.
common_error.why: Feedback is uncountable; use 'pieces of' for more than one.

vocabulary_list.definition: An important point or achievement in a project.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: Releasing the beta version is a big milestone for us.

common_error.wrong: We have reached to a milestone this week.
common_error.right: We have reached a milestone this week.
common_error.why: Reach is transitive; no preposition is needed after it.

vocabulary_list.definition: A plan or idea you present for others to approve.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: I submitted the proposal for the new testing tool yesterday.

common_error.wrong: I will proposal the new tool to the team.
common_error.right: I will propose the new tool to the team.
common_error.why: Propose is the verb; 'proposal' is only a noun.

vocabulary_list.definition: A person or group affected by or involved in the project.
vocabulary_list.example_in_story: We need to present the results to the stakeholder before Friday.

common_error.wrong: I will talk to the stakeholder about of the change.
common_error.right: I will talk to the stakeholder about the change.
common_error.why: 'About' is a preposition; no 'of' is needed after it.

grammar_points.explanation: The present perfect (have/has + past participle) describes past events that connect to the present moment.
grammar_points.usage_in_story: The learner uses it to report what they have already completed or experienced during the current sprint.
examples: I have finished the user stories for the login page.
Have you reviewed the sprint backlog yet?
We have completed two milestones so far this sprint.

grammar_points.explanation: The first conditional (if + present simple, will + base verb) describes real and likely future situations.
grammar_points.usage_in_story: The learner uses it to discuss what will happen if a condition is met or not met during the standup.
examples: If the blocker is cleared today, I can finish the task on time.
If we miss the deadline, the stakeholder will be unhappy.
If you give me feedback by noon, I will update the proposal.

grammar_points.explanation: Modals such as should, could, and ought to express suggestions or recommendations to the listener.
grammar_points.usage_in_story: The learner uses modals to ask Ethan for advice on how to handle a task or resolve a problem.
examples: Should I raise this blocker now or wait until tomorrow?
Could you advise me on which task to prioritize first?
I think we should update the stakeholder before the deadline.

key_milestones: Clarify progress update or sprint goal
closing_scenarios: Thanks, that answers my question.
Great, I understand the next step now.
Could you send me the details in writing?

suggested_prompts: Can I share my progress update before we start?
I think we should change the sprint goal for this week.
Could you help me clarify the deadline for the report?
